$comment: Removal ledger for shipped surfaces (CodySwannGT/lisa#3849). Enforced by
`bun run check:shipped-surface-removals`.
The copy lanes overwrite and never delete, and deepMergeWithArrayUnion
unions. So a template edit can ADD to a host's tree and can never remove
from it: the only mechanisms that reach an installed base are a
deletions.json entry and a migration under src/migrations/.
A removal therefore gets one of two dispositions, and they are opposites:
PROPAGATE - a deletions.json entry, for a path no host could have bound
to. The manifest is the record; nothing goes in this file.
RETAIN AND NOTIFY - an entry here, for a consumer-bindable executable
under scripts/ and for every removed named export. Propagating those
would delete a working host capability, which is how the ticket that
created this file was first mis-diagnosed.
Entry shape: { path, export?, issue?, note }. `path` is repo-relative,
inside a delivery lane. Omit `export` for a whole-file removal. `note` is
the consumer-facing part and must say what a host should DO - a blank one
is treated as no entry at all.
`baseline` is the window's lower bound: the first tag of the supported
major line. Advancing it retires obligations, so it is deliberately a
reviewable one-line edit here rather than something derived from a clock.
Entries are never pruned when the baseline moves past them - they are the
historical record a host on an older release still needs.

removals.note: Renamed to `fetchRunCandidates` in v4.26.1 and its shape changed with it: it reads a bounded page of runs (RUN_CANDIDATE_PAGE_SIZE) instead of `per_page: 1`, because scoring the newest run rather than the newest CONCLUSIVE one let a displaced, cancelled run overwrite the verdict of a run that tested everything. A host importing `fetchNewestRun` should import `fetchRunCandidates` and select with `runProducedEvidence(run, jobs)`; there is no drop-in single-run replacement, and asking for one would reintroduce the defect.

Removed in v4.31.0 together with the live-ruleset drift arm and the standing `administration:read` token it required. The constant only ever bounded the age of a snapshot that arm compared against, so with the arm gone it has no reading. A host that imported it - reported at least once, from a host-owned `scripts/check-required-checks-baseline.mjs` that Lisa never shipped - should drop the age check and the `--remote` npm scripts that fed it, or declare a fork of this script keeping the constant. The importer is NOT deleted for you: it is host-owned and may be wired to npm scripts, a workflow, and tests.

Removed in v4.31.0 with the live-ruleset drift arm. It compared the declared required contexts against the live ruleset over the GitHub API, which needs `administration:read` and therefore a personal access token in a permanent repository secret. There is no replacement by design - the remaining check reads the reviewed snapshot in `.github/required-checks.json`. A host calling it should delete the call and keep the snapshot transcribed.

Removed in v4.31.0 with the live-ruleset drift arm, for the same reason as `compareRulesetBaseline`: it was the API call that required `administration:read`. A host calling it should delete the call; the required contexts now come from `.github/required-checks.json`, transcribed byte for byte.
